newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway sets up group to manage Petroleum Fund.
newsitem.headline: Norway sets up group to manage Petroleum Fund.

text.p: Norway's central bank, Norges Bank, said on Thursday it had appointed a project group to prepare for the management of the Government Petroleum Fund.
The project will result in a separate entity in Norges Bank that will begin operations from January 1, 1998, the bank said in a statement.
"The Section for Asset Management will report to the central bank governor and operate separately from Norges Bank's foreign exchange and monetary policy functions," it said.
On June 20 parliament endorsed a proposal in the revised national budget for part of the Government Petroleum Fund to be invested in foreign equities.

Norway is expected to have a budget surplus of more than 57 billion crowns in 1997 due to revenues from the country's booming oil and gas industry. This surplus is put into the Government Petroleum Fund for investment to secure the future and pension payments for an increasingly aged population.

Norges Bank manages the fund based on guidelines issued by the Finance Ministry. New guidelines are expected to be presented in the 1998 budget in October, with investment in equities starting the following January.
The bank said it would use external managers -- both Norwegian and international -- for equity investments. Mandates for management will be announced in July.
